why: The standard way to shrug off a bad day.
Explains why someone keeps arguing or goes ahead with a dare: pride. It differs from the pool's ato ni hikenai, which is about a situation, not saving face.

literal: not even a place to step
why: The everyday description of a messy room, said by parents and roommates.

english: awkward silence; can't keep the conversation going
why: The core idiom for awkward silences on dates, in elevators and with a new coworker.

romaji: nokorimono ni wa fuku ga aru
kana: のこりものにはふくがある
english: the last one left may be the lucky one
why: Said cheerfully whenever someone gets the last piece or picks last.
Constant in food talk at meals and on TV. The negative, hashi ga susumanai (no appetite), is also common.

kana: やすものがいのぜにうしない
english: buying cheap costs more in the end
why: The standard thing to say when a bargain breaks.

romaji: kenka suru hodo naka ga ii
ja: 喧嘩するほど仲がいい
kana: けんかするほどなかがいい
english: people who argue a lot are actually close
why: Said when teasing bickering friends, siblings or couples.

romaji: hara ga hette wa ikusa wa dekinu
ja: 腹が減っては戦はできぬ
kana: はらがへってはいくさはできぬ
literal: you can't fight a battle hungry
english: eat first, then get to work
englishIdiom: an army marches on its stomach
why: Said jokingly before a meal break at work or study.

romaji: yoso wa yoso uchi wa uchi
ja: よそはよそ、うちはうち
kana: よそはよそ、うちはうち
literal: other homes are other homes, ours is ours
english: other families do it their way, we do it ours
englishIdiom: if your friends jumped off a bridge, would you?
why: The parents' classic reply to 'but everyone else has one', and widely quoted.

literal: I'd like to see your parents' faces
why: The stock grumble about rude kids and young people, said out loud or muttered.

ja: おいしいところを持っていく
kana: おいしいところをもっていく
english: grab the credit or the big moment
why: A staple of casual and variety-TV talk: 'zenbu oishii tokoro motte ikareta' (they took all the credit).

romaji: ishi no ue ni mo sannen
kana: いしのうえにもさんねん
literal: even on a cold stone, three years
english: stick with it and it pays off
englishIdiom: Rome wasn't built in a day
why: The classic advice to stay at a new job or hobby long enough to see results.

kana: どんぐりのせいくらべ
englishIdiom: six of one, half a dozen of the other
why: Said of candidates or teams with nothing to choose between them. Pool's dotchi mo dotchi is about both being at fault, which is different.

englishIdiom: no room to swing a cat
why: The modest way to describe your own garden, flat or yard: 'neko no hitai hodo no niwa'.

romaji: kusai mono ni futa o suru
polite: kusai mono ni futa o shimasu
kana: くさいものにふたをする
literal: put a lid on the smelly thing
english: hide an embarrassing problem instead of fixing it
why: Used for companies, schools and families hushing up a problem.

english: it would weigh on your conscience
englishIdiom: it would keep me up at night
why: The reason people give for helping anyway: 'misuteru no mo nezame ga warui shi'. Pool's ki ga togameru is guilt after the fact; this is guilt you would feel.
